paragraphs: The signal that this is worth trying first is a willingness to turn 'what do I want to find out' into a clear research question and to check whether the wording, the sample source and the answers really support the conclusion, rather than chasing attractive charts.

Judge research interest and working conditions separately. Questionnaire testing, data cleaning and method records often need repeated revision; travel, interviewer coordination and project timing should be checked against the specific post, without assuming that everyone does long-term fieldwork.

First choose the task object: survey design emphasises measurement and sampling, collection management emphasises interviewers and completion status, and data analysis emphasises coding, statistics and interpretation. This occupation may cover several stages, and conducting interviews is not the same as independently owning the research design.

For the safe experience, use the six fictional book-exchange records in the entry module F1, judge the eight claims independently, then revise the original draft in two places each for the F2 A and B feedback and fill in F3. Pen and paper are enough; do not contact real residents, collect private information or fabricate interviewees.
What kind of person is survey research suited to?

See whether you are willing to turn a research question into a testable questionnaire and sample design, trace missing data and the denominator, and state clearly what the material supports and what it does not. Communication involves clients, interviewers and analytical colleagues; patience in revision and evidence discipline are more worth experiencing than simply liking to ask questions.
This is a career exploration screening, not hiring, a statistics competence certification or a personality diagnosis. It also needs to be combined with training background and real post requirements.

More specific signals are: being able to state the target population and the question first, then check whether the items make respondents understand the same thing; checking completion status, coding rules and the analytical denominator, and going back to the material when conflicts appear instead of hiding them. On receiving feedback, being able to say which rule was changed and why, and leaving unconfirmed samples and explanations as unknown. Organising the method record on time and being honest about your own statistical experience are also important signs of reliable cooperation.

Signals needing caution include: equating more answers collected with representativeness, treating a significant result as the only value, filling missing answers in at will as the expected answer, or wanting only to produce charts without explaining the process. Also assess public communication, repeated quality checks and fieldwork arrangements separately; liking social contact cannot replace questionnaire and statistics training, and disliking a lot of social contact cannot automatically rule out the analysis direction.

After finishing, record which denominator judgment went wrong, what specific revisions the two sets of feedback produced, and whether you are willing to check one more set of material. A single fictional exercise only supports the next exploration step and cannot impersonate a real survey or a professional qualification.

The U.S. occupational identity on this page is O*NET-SOC 19-3022.00 Survey Researchers: planning, developing and conducting surveys and analysing and interpreting the material. It may include social science researchers focused on questionnaire design or survey team supervision; market research, statisticians and interviewer execution each have their own boundaries.

Material inputs include the research objective, the target population, the available sample frame, the questionnaire, the collection method and existing data. First distinguish the population you want to describe from the population you can actually reach; convenience-collected answers cannot automatically represent the population.

Questionnaire judgments must return to the research question: are the wording, the options, the routing and the time frame consistent, and does an item lead the respondent or mix several questions? The editorial exercise checks the task text and the coding first and does not treat your own preference as the respondent's actual answer.

Outputs include tables, charts, fact statements and analytical reports on the survey technique and results. The questionnaire version, the variable rules and the method notes should be kept so colleagues can review how the data produced the conclusion.

When monitoring collection, check the sample completion status and the response calculation, distinguishing complete, partially complete, refused and unknown eligibility. A rate must have a clear numerator, denominator and rule, and a high completion rate alone cannot declare that the material has no bias.

Survey researchers collaborate with clients, interviewers, method and analysis staff. They may arrange surveys, evaluate collection and review interview work; design changes and external publication are confirmed by the actual project leads, and knowing the software does not let you change the basis yourself.

Occupational activities include background research, understanding client needs, selecting information sources and procedures, and continuously updating survey methods. An internship or assistant task may touch one part of this and does not automatically prove that you can independently own a whole project.

At delivery, record the questionnaire development, collection, sampling and statistical weighting decisions, and explain the limitations and unanswered questions. A public report does not mean that raw identifying material may be published; data use must be checked against the law, institutional arrangements and the research agreement.

Survey design and survey implementation are two connected work lines: the first determines measurement and sample, the second puts the plan into collection, quality checks and analysis. What follows is an editorial process based on the tasks of this occupation, not a uniform national operating procedure.
Survey design and pretesting line
Clarify the question and the population → check the sample frame → write the items → pretest → revise the procedure → keep the method record
An executable questionnaire, sample design and method notes
Implementation and data analysis line
Organise collection → monitor status → code and clean → analyse and tabulate → explain limitations → keep the method record
Checkable data, summary charts and an analytical report
Common professional foundation
Research question · measurement · sampling · coding · statistical interpretation · method records · participant protection
What is the difference between questionnaire design and interviewer execution?

The design side decides what must be measured, whom to ask and how to ask; interviewers contact, ask and record according to the confirmed procedure, and collection management handles coordination and quality tracking. Survey researchers may supervise these stages, and the specific division depends on the project; the table below compares responsibilities and cannot be used to define a uniform job grade.
Core purpose
Form a measurement and sample design that can answer the research question, clarifying the survey subjects, the items and the interpretation boundary.
Obtain answers under the confirmed procedure and record completion status accurately, without changing what respondents express.
Main object and basis
The research objective, the target population, the sample frame, existing research and questionnaire pretest results.
The confirmed questionnaire, contact procedure, collection arrangements, interview records and participant notes.
Core process
Background research, designing and testing the wording, selecting the sample and mode, then reviewing the measurement and analysis plan.
Receive training, contact and ask according to the procedure, record answers and refusals, and report anomalies and progress.
Main outputs
Questionnaire versions, sampling and collection plans, coding rules and analysis method notes.
Raw answers, complete or partially complete status, anomaly records and collection progress material.
Responsible subject
The research and method leads confirm the design and interpretation, and survey researchers propose, test and record decisions within the actual division of work.
Interviewers are responsible for accurate execution and recording; questions beyond the procedure go to the collection supervisor or research lead for confirmation.
How support works
Clarify the needs with the client and verify with the collection team whether the items, the procedure and the resources are feasible.
Report comprehension difficulties and execution anomalies through the procedure, and without confirmation do not change items or choose answers for respondents.
Delivery boundaries
A sound design does not guarantee the absence of non-response or measurement error, and the analysis must still check the data and the limitations.
Completing one interview does not prove that the sample represents the population and does not grant authority to publish research conclusions independently.
Key occupational judgments

Every judgment must be traceable to the research objective, the sample and the records. What follows is an editorially designed work self-check; you cannot jump from one rate, model result or chart straight to a conclusion about the whole population.
Do the items and options measure the same clear question?
Where does the actual sample come from, and how does it differ from the target population?
How are complete, partially complete and refused defined, and is the denominator consistent?
After receiving quality feedback, which rule should be revised and how is it reviewed?

Locate the item number, record or calculation rule first, then explain how the revision affects the conclusion. Keep the original and the reasons, and do not merely polish the wording; changing the real survey procedure requires confirmation by the project lead.
Does the data use exceed the participant notes and institutional authority?

Check the data source, identifying information, processing purpose and tool permission separately; a new purpose cannot be assumed to be allowed merely because the original file is accessible. AAPOR provides a professional ethics reference, and the actual legal and institutional requirements must be checked per project.
After the report is delivered, which method decisions and limitations should be retained?
Design | Clarify the research objective and population | Understand client needs and existing research, and determine the questions to answer, the data sources and the survey scope.
Design | Questionnaire development and pretesting | Suggest and test wording, options and procedures, and record revisions after finding comprehension or measurement problems.
Implementation | Coordinate collection and interviewer work | Plan and coordinate single or multiple surveys, organise training and procedure communication, and review the collection work.
Monitoring | Sample status and collection quality | Check sample completion and response calculations, evaluate interview material and follow up anomalies.
Analysis | Coding, statistics and interpretation | Process the data according to the objective and data rules, produce tables, charts and fact summaries, and explain limitations.

Delivery | Method records and professional updating | Record the questionnaire, collection, sampling and weighting decisions, keep researching survey methods, and do not replace method notes with charts.
Section title | The work environment and working style of survey researchers

BLS describes U.S. survey researchers as mostly office-based, possibly analysing independently or working with a research team, and sometimes travelling to interview the public. Most work full time on regular schedules, and the specific project still needs checking.

Common organisations and locations | The U.S. material lists employers such as professional and technical services, education, research and development and non-profit organisations, including the self-employed. Office analysis and on-site interviewing are different settings; the two historical Chinese announcements involve a Renmin University Beijing internship and an Ocean University Laoshan research assistant respectively and do not represent all post locations or employment forms.

Work materials and tools | Research briefs, literature, sample frames, questionnaire versions, interview status and coded data are common inputs. Statistics, tabulation and survey systems serve methods and quality checks; specific software is learned per post requirement, and buying software, equipment or training is not treated as a general admission qualification.

Survey design, collection and analysis must connect: a change of items may affect coding and comparability, and collection anomalies need to be fed back to the method lead. Record the confirmed versions, responsible people and pending clarifications per project.

Scheduling and intensity | The U.S. description of mostly full-time, regular hours cannot be assumed to apply to every project. Travel for interviews, concentrated collection, training and report deadlines affect personal arrangements; the Renmin University internship announcement required at least three working days per week, which represents only that historical project. Ask about the real time, place and scope of change before choosing.

In communication, state the problem, the record number and the effect on results. Facing client expectations, still distinguish what has been observed, the method limitations and the explanations still to be verified.

Review and the responsibility chain | Survey researchers may analyse, supervise and propose method suggestions, but procedure changes, data access and publication authority in a real project are defined by the institutional division of work. If sample, wording or statistical basis conflicts appear, keep the original records and refer them to the corresponding responsible person; a generative summary cannot replace substantive judgment.

Quality and occupational requirements | Observable quality is whether the questionnaire is clear, whether the material and coding are consistent, whether the calculations can be reproduced, and whether the conclusions are constrained by evidence. Proactively stating missing data and sample limitations is more reliable than hiding unfavourable results. A fictional exercise can observe initial interest, and professional qualification still needs training, real tasks and feedback.

Survey researchers plan, develop and conduct surveys, analyse and interpret the material, clarify objectives, test questionnaires, monitor collection and produce result summaries and method records. The duties may cover design, collection management and analysis; interview execution and population inference must be distinguished by the actual division of work and the evidence.
Coordinate the procedures, records and compliance tasks of clinical research; general survey experience cannot replace clinical project training and authorization.
Study organisational problems and processes and propose efficiency and management improvements; research communication shares a foundation, but the delivery object and responsibility differ.
Study markets, consumer demand and competition to support marketing decisions; a questionnaire is only one possible information source.

paragraphs: This occupation: survey design and methods
Clarify the research question, measurement and sample design, test the questionnaire and record the sampling and weighting decisions.
The focus is whether the material can answer the question, which requires stating the target population, sampling and measurement limitations; it is not just writing the items smoothly.
Willing to trace the problem definition, test comprehension differences and accept several rounds of revision.
This occupation: collection management and data quality
Coordinate collection, review interview work, check sample status, coding and response calculations, then produce a reviewable summary.
The focus is plan execution and material consistency; interviewers completing interviews cannot directly stand in for population interpretation.
Willing to handle repeated checks and anomaly communication and to record rules and versions clearly.
Clinical research coordinators
It involves clinical research procedures and compliance records, and ordinary questionnaire project experience does not automatically grant clinical task authority.
Interested in research execution and participant management, and willing to check the target institution's clinical training requirements.
Management consulting analysts
The output is advice on organisational processes and management, and one survey report cannot prove all consulting ability.
More focused on organisational problems and implementing improvements, and willing to build process diagnosis and advisory communication.
Market research analysts specialising in marketing
Facing consumer demand, competition and marketing decisions, where a survey is only one method; market and business interpretation ability must be built.
Wanting to apply research results to business problems, and willing to learn the market context and decision-making use.
Financial analysts
The O*NET object linked here is financial quantitative analysis, delivering investment, valuation or risk models; it is not the same as direct promotion from a survey occupation.
Willing to build finance, mathematics and modelling and to verify the transition with the target outputs.
How do you choose among survey design, quality management and adjacent occupations?

First distinguish the tasks inside this occupation from independent adjacent occupations. Design concerns what to ask, whom to ask and how to infer; collection management concerns obtaining material through the procedure and its quality. Clinical coordination, management consulting, market research and financial quantitative analysis each have their own objects and deliverables; sharing tables or interviews does not mean they can be swapped directly.

Use the six fictional records first to experience denominators, missing data and conclusion boundaries, then judge whether you prefer design, checking or interpretation. When moving to an adjacent job, prove the new ability with the target tasks' outputs; the original method experience can serve as a base but does not automatically meet the professional knowledge, project authority or employer conditions.

The process for this occupation is compiled from O*NET 19-3022.00 and BLS; the four adjacent directions use their own O*NET profiles. The fit signals and the experience order are editorial suggestions, not official hiring standards. The local 'financial analyst' link is explicitly limited to 13-2099.01 financial quantitative analysis; the specific Chinese qualifications and post conditions are checked separately.

After choosing the task, judge whether AI assists the questionnaire draft, the coding or the analysis, and check the input permission, the errors and the human responsibility separately; a general trend cannot replace analysis of the specific post.

At the technical ability level, you can try using text tools to organise question lists, propose alternative wording or write coding drafts. These are editorial suggested uses and do not prove that the questionnaire measures better. You must return to the research objective, the original records and human testing; generating reasonable text is not the same as a representative sample or correct analysis.

Questionnaire drafts, open-ended coding and simulated answers are different tasks. The first two must be verified for their effect on measurement and classification; simulated material must be kept separate from people's actual answers. The editorial exercise uses only the fictional records in the task text and cannot add generated answers into the completion count.

At the actual adoption level, this page obtained no separate representative AI usage rate or net time-saving study for survey researchers. Professional discussion, cross-occupation exposure indicators and one institution's tool trial cannot replace an adoption share. The task, the input, the human check and the deployment context should be stated separately, and technical feasibility cannot be used to infer widespread use.

First determine the research question and the available materials, check the output, record the human changes, and then decide whether it can be delivered. Real data, procedure changes and public reports must be confirmed by the responsible person with authority on the project; the control process below is an editorial application, not a new statutory licence.

The ILO cross-occupation research assesses potential task exposure and notes that work transformation is more likely; it is not a substitution rate or a probability of unemployment for this occupation.

The O*NET tasks for this occupation include questionnaire testing, collection monitoring, material analysis and method records, but they do not provide improvement percentages after AI use. Being able to draft questions still requires checking the actual measurement, sample and interpretation.

Next, test the tool against the specific task: does it help find omissions, does it introduce errors, can the human review be traced? Keep the record of the model's actual use and non-use, then observe the working conditions, and do not treat tool output as a transfer of research responsibility.

At the employment outcome level, the precise U.S. projection for this occupation falls 4.8% over 2025—2035, with average annual openings of about 600. BLS notes that methods such as data mining and big data may reduce the need for traditional surveys; the projection includes many factors and cannot isolate job losses caused independently by generative AI. Personal opportunity and the Chinese market need separate evidence.

BLS2025 through 2035 United States SOC19-3022 overall projection for survey researchers in this occupation: 9,800 people in the 2025 base period, 9,300 at the end of 2035, an official net decrease of 500, a change of −4.8%; average annual openings of 600 include transfers, exits and replacements and are not net additions or current hiring. The headcounts are converted from thousands and keep the original table's precision, and the growth rate cannot be recomputed from the two rounded endpoints; the projection covers the self-employed and others and so differs from the OEWS wage-earner population, and it cannot be extended to a generative AI independent substitution rate, Chinese projections or an individual's probability of unemployment.
How will AI change the tasks and responsibilities of survey researchers?

Text, coding and analysis assistance can be explored, but questionnaire validity, sample source, missing-data handling and the scope of conclusions still need human checking. Cross-occupation exposure is not a substitution rate for this occupation, and this page has no representative adoption share or reviewable FermatMind task score. Test the specific task first, then decide how to use it.

Below, the tasks of this occupation, the employment projection, cross-occupation research and generic risk methods are listed separately. Check the research object, the year and the scope first; global exposure, occupational decline and tool capability cannot be converted into one another. All operational suggestions for this occupation need real data and human review, and matters without figures remain unknown.
United States SOC19-3022 survey researchers for this occupation; the 2025 base period and the 2025–2035 overall projection, not adjacent occupations such as market research.
A projection of the occupational total, not a measure of generative AI's independent effect; it cannot be extrapolated to a Chinese or personal probability of unemployment.

BLS notes that related technologies improve market research efficiency and may reduce the need for traditional telephone and face-to-face surveys; this is not the same as generative AI replacing the whole occupation.
That explanation is not a substitution share that can be attributed on its own, nor can it be extrapolated to China.
Cross-domain risks of generative AI such as information reliability and privacy
NIST provides a general risk management approach; this page treats checking materials, reviewing outputs and keeping records as editorial applications.
The voluntary cross-domain framework is not a regulation specific to survey researchers and provides no accident or adoption rate for this occupation.
Can AI directly design a valid questionnaire?

It can propose a draft, but validity must return to the research objective, the item meaning, the options and pretesting. O*NET lists suggesting and testing wording as a task of this occupation, and generated text cannot be treated as a test result. The specific way it assists is an editorial suggestion, with no verified improvement percentage.
Is the global exposure share the substitution rate for survey researchers?

No. The ILO cross-occupation task exposure indicator describes potential technological impact, not actual adoption or a probability of unemployment for this occupation. This page does not enter the global share as a score for this occupation and does not infer from exposure that a particular person will lose their job.
Is the 4.8% decline the jobs AI eliminated?

No. The precise occupational projection includes many factors and cannot separate out the generative AI effect on its own; the average annual 600 openings come from replacement and other demand and cannot be treated as net annual growth or a substitution figure.
Does being able to draft questions mean being able to design research?
Will existing big data eliminate all surveys?

BLS describes the background of methods such as data mining and the change in traditional collection needs; it does not prove that all surveys will be eliminated. Compare the specific research question, whether the material can cover the target population and the method limitations, and do not mix big data and generative AI as the same kind of evidence.
Can AI fill in missing answers?

This exercise does not allow generated answers to be treated as actual completion records. Methodologically, the data source, coding and simulation purpose must be stated; this limitation is an editorial exercise rule, not a specific law that NIST issued for this occupation. Keep the missing data and the human review records.
What should be checked before using real survey material?

Check the processing purpose, the material permission, the identifying information and the tool's storage purpose first, then arrange output checking and confirmation by the responsible person. NIST is a general risk reference; the specific law, participant agreement and institutional rules still have to be checked separately. Tool access does not prove the right to upload.

Insufficient evidence: a nationally comparable wage distribution for survey researchers in China. Two historical institutional announcements were checked, one CGSS internship with an undisclosed allowance amount and one adjacent research assistant post disclosing a basic salary; they are not a national sample and cannot be compared directly with the U.S. statistics for this occupation.

When comparing posts, check the contracting entity, the employment form, the basic salary or internship allowance, performance pay, social insurance and housing fund and the work requirements separately; similar job titles do not guarantee the same duties or statistical object.

Basic salary, separately calculated performance pay and personal take-home income are different quantities. The Ocean University announcement gives no after-tax value or uniform performance amount, so 8,000 yuan per month cannot be treated directly as take-home income or extrapolated to national master's-level pay.

The Ocean University 2025-06-06 announcement recruited a research assistant for the Global New Quality Productive Forces Research Centre, through labour dispatch, master's degree or above, basic salary 8,000 yuan per month with performance calculated separately by workload; the deadline was 2025-06-20. The duties include research data analysis, reports and project affairs, and this is an adjacent post rather than an exact mapping of the U.S. occupation. 2025 pre-tax annual average wage for the broad professional and technical personnel post in China's above-scale enterprises: 155,491 yuan per year. The official definition covers personnel engaged specifically in scientific research and professional technical work; the author references it as a condition only when the person actually carries research professional duties such as survey design, measurement or research analysis and the unit is included in the statistics, and interview execution, liaison or administrative affairs are not automatically included because of a similar name. The coverage is enterprise legal persons in 16 industry categories included by size, qualification or quota conditions, not all universities, research institutes or all urban units; it includes individual income tax, social insurance and housing fund deductions, and it is not the median, starting pay or a personal range for survey researchers and does not replace the Ocean University dispatch basic salary or the Renmin University internship allowance.

The Renmin University CGSS 2026-05-27 internship announcement lists tasks such as questionnaire standardisation, system testing, training and liaison, with an allowance consisting of basic pay plus performance but no amount given. The published attendance period runs from 2026-06-01 to 09-30 with at least three working days per week; that period has ended, so it cannot be used to confirm that it is still recruiting.

values: F1 | Original fictional book exchange material

All editorially fictional, not a real survey. The objective is only to check the rules; all six records are known to be eligible and come from convenience practice material, with no probability sampling, weighting or population representativeness. Question: if a book exchange event were held next month, would you be willing to take part? Options: willing, not willing, not sure yet, prefer not to answer.

Records: 01 complete / willing; 02 complete / not willing; 03 complete / this item missing; 04 complete / willing; 05 partially complete / this item unanswered; 06 refused / this item unanswered. Rule: completeness follows the status in the task text, and a missing item does not change the status. The valid answers to this item are only willing or not willing in the complete records; missing, partial and refused are not recorded as no.
F2 | The task and two independent feedback sets

First judge the eight claims item by item: (a) eligible records 6; (b) complete 4; (c) valid answers to this item among the complete ones 3; (d) willing 2; (e) the willing proportion of valid answers 2/3=66.7%; (f) missing may be recorded as not willing; (g) the six records prove that most of the community or the country is willing; (h) two AI-generated records may be recorded as actual completions. Write supported or unsupported with the basis for each item.

Draft to be revised: 'the willing proportion of valid answers is 50%; missing is treated as not willing; this proves that most community residents are willing; AI is used to fill in two completed questionnaires.' A feedback: check the valid denominator and the missing-data handling, one change each. B feedback: independently check the interpretation scope and the simulated material from the same draft, one change each. At least two changes per version, keeping the before and after and the basis; do not use version A as the draft for version B. F3 records the source, your own outputs, the given feedback, the original, the A and B changes and reasons, and the actual AI use (write none if unused), with no real-person information collected.
Reference answer | Five supported, three unsupported

(a) to (e) supported; (f) to (h) not supported. The completeness proportion is defined as 4/6=66.7%, which is only the completion proportion customised for this exercise, not a general official AAPOR response rate. Among the complete records, valid answers are 3 (01, 02, 04) and willing is 2 (01, 04), so the valid willing proportion is 2/3=66.7%; 2/4=50% is another quantity using all complete records as the denominator and cannot be labelled the valid answer proportion. Missing for 03 is not the same as not willing, and the partial 05 and refused 06 cannot be added to the valid denominator for this item.

Version A, two points: 50% changed to 66.7%, noting the 01, 02, 04 denominator; missing changed to keeping the missing data rather than coding it as no. Version B, two points: community majority changed to describing only the three valid fictional records without extrapolating to the population; AI filling in completions changed to not treating generated material as actual participants. The two versions focus on different problems, the unrevised items still need integrating, and the final draft must correct all four points together. F3 reference: original fiction on this page, your own paper judgments and the two revisions, feedback from the task text, no real people or third-party material, and write none if AI was not actually used.
Exercise boundaries and the four work products

Pen and paper are enough; do not contact real people, collect private material or add simulated participants. Four work products: (a) the eight first judgments and three denominator calculations; (b) the A and B versions with two changes each and the final integrated draft; (c) the F3 source and actual tool record; (d) the seven-day review and the next method learning question. The reference answer is for checking; answer independently first, and do not impersonate a formal survey, an employer evaluation or a professional qualification.
